### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **43** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-schema-config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 76e4c2cdf1e6f411b98f6520c0a2bc83ebbd68c4`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-schema-config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 76e4c2cdf1e6f411b98f6520c0a2bc83ebbd68c4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0d1bc61b4315b8c59d9f43cdf11bbfda09c6eec5` — the merge of head `951de4cfa86a02f5967412f92f83ef28b01e2f13` into base `76e4c2cdf1e6f411b98f6520c0a2bc83ebbd68c4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0d1bc61b4315b8c59d9f43cdf11bbfda09c6eec5 && git checkout 0d1bc61b4315b8c59d9f43cdf11bbfda09c6eec5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 76e4c2cdf1e6f411b98f6520c0a2bc83ebbd68c4 951de4cfa86a02f5967412f92f83ef28b01e2f13 && git checkout -B drift-repro 76e4c2cdf1e6f411b98f6520c0a2bc83ebbd68c4 && git merge --no-ff 951de4cfa86a02f5967412f92f83ef28b01e2f13

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 76e4c2cdf1e6f411b98f6520c0a2bc83ebbd68c4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 76e4c2cdf1e6f411b98f6520c0a2bc83ebbd68c4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `9c8e1977acae130ecfa307ccf9d859fd514f8d01`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and only these: card #30967 with every comment (triage 6687843375, serial wait 6702286087, seat options 6710967585, ruling record 6718355623 (option A), claim 6718397620, dev report 6719252885); the PR #31448 body, its file list (24 files) and the net diff `origin/main...9c8e1977`; the head's check-runs. Vendor behaviour was read in the published `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 source (npm tarball, read only, nothing run).

**Gates on this head, as read:** 55 check-runs: 16 success, 16 skipped, 4 failure, 19 cancelled, 0 in progress. The four failures are `Check Changeset` twice (128675741378, 128676239396): "Introduced at `minor` or above … Under `none` the level is `patch`". The other two are the `TypeScript Type Check` and `Lint & Repo Gates` aggregators, which failed because their lanes were cancelled. All of Test Core 1–8, Build Core, Build Docs, Live E2E UI and the type-check and lint lanes were **cancelled** when 53145b30 was pushed on top. That push changes only the two bump lines of the changeset. So on this head, no test, type-check, lint or build family has answered. The dev's local runs are the dev's claims, not gate verdicts. The judgments below come from the diff and the vendor source.

### ① Derived judgments

(a) **Default off, no new writers: right.**
- `allow_idp_initiated` and `allow_jit` are `Field.boolean({ defaultValue: false, trackHistory: true })` (sys-sso-provider.object.ts). They reach the vendor as `additionalFields` with `defaultValue: false, input: true` (sso-sign-in-options.ts `SSO_PROVIDER_SIGN_IN_FIELDS`).
- In the vendor source, `parseSSOProviderAdditionalFields` is the only door for these fields. `/sso/register` sits behind plugin-auth's platform-admin registration gate (#10009). `/sso/update-provider` sits behind `sessionMiddleware` and `checkProviderAccess`: the provider's owner, or an org owner or admin when the row carries `organizationId`. plugin-auth's before-hook also refuses a held caller there (auth-manager-before-hook.ts, ADR-0069 D3).
- The generic data layer stays read-only (`apiMethods: ['get','list']`), and nothing in the diff adds an engine write to `sys_sso_provider`.
- These are exactly the people who write a provider today. No new writer population.

(b) **Refused when off, scoped per provider: right.**
- SAML: the vendor reads `options.saml.allowIdpInitiated` once per Response, inside `processSAMLResponse` → `validateInResponseTo`, which runs at request time. A plain getter on the options object is therefore read per request.
- The scope is opened only for a `POST /sso/saml2/sp/acs/:providerId`. plugin-auth takes the id from the same path segment the vendor uses as `ctx.params.providerId` to load the provider. A path the classifier does not take (a trailing `/`, a GET carrying a body, an `auth.api.*` call) runs with no scope, and the getter then answers false. That is fail-closed.
- `AsyncLocalStorage.run` isolates concurrent requests, and there is a two-scope `Promise.all` pin. 1.7.12 has one SAML ACS route, and the provider comes from the path, so one provider's toggle cannot reach another provider's Response. The "another provider's toggle" pin covers this.
- OIDC: `bounceIfIdpInitiated` reads `provider.oidcConfig.allowIdpInitiated` per provider row, through `adapter.findOne`. The adapter's read half sets that member from the provider's own column, so the toggle stays per row. The shared `/sso/callback` with no state still answers `invalid_state`.
- Off: SAML still answers 302 `unsolicited_response` and OIDC 302 `state_not_found`, both pinned.

(c) **`invite_only` refusal: right, and it happens before any row is written.**
- The gate runs in `validateUserInfo`, which better-auth's `internalAdapter.createUser` calls before the user insert. A refusal therefore writes no user, and so no account or session.
- `decideAudienceAdmission`'s provider branch is gated only when all of these hold: `ssoProvider` is present (source `sso-oidc` or `sso-saml`), `allowJit` is off, and the posture is a valid `invite_only`. The bootstrap and pending-invitation carve-outs still admit.
- The unchanged cases hold in code: `oidcProviders` (oauth) never sets `ssoProvider`; `email_domain`, `open` and an invalid posture skip the gate; `link-account` and sign-in are never judged; an unreadable row reads as off. The matrix and both protocol harnesses pin them.

(d) **Every change is audited: right.**
- Both fields are `trackHistory`. Adapter writes go through `withSystemContext`, which stamps `authSystemWriteContext()`, so the ledger row names the human who called update-provider (#4586).
- The plugin-audit pin (old and new values, plus the activity line) drives the engine directly rather than the vendor door. The attribution seam is shared with every other better-auth write, so that is acceptable.

(e) **A stored blob member cannot override the column: right.**
- `applyIdpInitiatedToOidcConfigOnRead` always overwrites the member from the column. A missing or unselected column reads false.
- The strip on write runs on create, update and updateMany. So when update-provider's `mergeOIDCConfig` spreads the injected value back in, it is not stored.

Findings:
- **should-fix — packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts:281-283.**
  - The **Edit Sign-In Options** action pre-fills `allowIdpInitiated` and `allowJit` from the row (`defaultFromRow`).
  - Below better-auth these columns hold `1` or `0`, which sso-sign-in-options.ts `storedOn` documents. A row that predates the columns may hold `NULL`.
  - The vendor's update body types both as `z.boolean()`, and anything else is refused 400.
  - Every pin posts `true` or `false` directly. None drives the action from a stored row.
  - The changeset names this action as *the* escape hatch for existing `invite_only` deployments. Pin, or measure on a booted console, the body the action sends for a row holding `1`, `0` and `NULL`.
- **nit — sso-sign-in-options.ts:174.**
  - The vendor's `computeProviderAuthenticationFingerprint` hashes `oidcConfig`, and the injected member is now part of it.
  - So an OIDC sign-in that starts before the deploy, or before a toggle flip, and finishes after it fails once with an invalid-state redirect. This is fail-closed. A docs line would do.
- **nit — register-sso-provider.ts:223 and :325.**
  - The Setup bridges register with the caller's active `organizationId`. The vendor's `checkProviderAccess` therefore also lets that org's owners and admins flip `allowJit`.
  - This is not new: they could already edit the provider. But sso.mdx's "the people who can change a provider today" could name them.

### ② Semver level

- **must-fix — .changeset/30967-sso-sign-in-options.md:2-3 and :9.**
  - As committed, the head grades both packages `minor` under `Metadata-protocol: none`. `Check Changeset` is red twice on this head for exactly that.
  - The fix being pushed (53145b30: `patch` + `none`) clears the gate but resolves it the wrong way. The kind is not `none`.
  - This diff changes the meaning of an authorable key: `auth.audience.posture: 'invite_only'` (`system.AuthConfig.audience`). Its published spec contract on `main` lists "an operator-registered identity provider" among the operator acts that admit under `invite_only`, at packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts:393-398 and :421-430.
  - After this diff, such a provider admits an uninvited person only with `allowJit` on. The default meaning of the posture for every deployment with an IdP has moved.
  - That is the gate's own definition of `Metadata-protocol: semantic` ("the meaning or default of an authorable key changes → `minor`"). The same surface already carries a semantic precedent: `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.audience-posture-default-invite-only.ts`.
  - Fix: declare `Metadata-protocol: semantic` in the PR body and in the changeset, and keep `minor` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/platform-objects`, which the gate accepts for `semantic`. The two new columns, the action and the REST body members are `none`-class on their own, but the posture change decides the kind.
- **Clause-② line:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is present in the PR body and the changeset, and it is right for items 1 and 2, which are new toggles that widen who can sign in, default off.
- **Behaviour-change statement:** the ruling's requirement is met. The changeset's **Behaviour change for existing deployments** paragraph says plainly that uninvited SSO sign-ins under `invite_only` (the default) are now refused with `SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED` and that no user is created. It names the per-provider `allowJit` escape hatch, with both the Setup path and the REST call, and lists the unchanged cases. One caveat: with `Clause-② yes`, the release notes file this entry under "new capabilities", not "action required". The prose paragraph is the operator's only signal, so it must stay as written.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report's `open_questions` is empty. Its two out-of-scope flags:

- **should-fix (escalated to the seat) — ADR-0011 not edited.**
  - The behaviour is right. `edit_sso_sign_in_options` (sys-sso-provider.object.ts:261) declares no `ai` block, so it is not exposed, and by bucket H's own test ("changes … who can sign in") it would be human-only anyway.
  - The flag's `carrier: none` is wrong. docs/adr/0011-actions-as-ai-tools.md:372-382 records that the tree holds "one more identity action", `list_platform_admins`, "the one identity action that postdates the assessment".
  - After this diff there are two, and the ADR says its table "lives only here; a reviewer of `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/**` reads it".
  - The bucket is assigned by maintainer ruling on a governed surface, so it belongs to the seat: an ADR-0011 amendment that assesses `sys_sso_provider.edit_sso_sign_in_options` (or at least lists it as unassessed), filed as a follow-up card. It is not owed in this PR.
- **nit (accepted) — Setup register bridges do not forward the toggles.**
  - `/admin/sso/register` and `register-saml` (register-sso-provider.ts:223 and :325) send named fields only. A provider registered from Setup therefore starts with both toggles off, which is the ruled default, and is then edited with the action.
  - This fails closed and is stated in the PR and the docs. The vendor's own `/sso/register` takes both members. No carrier is needed beyond the S3 pin above.
- **should-fix (escalated to the seat) — the published spec now misstates `invite_only`.**
  - packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts:393-398 (`audiencePermitsSelfRegistration`) and :426-430 (`AudienceConfigSchema.posture`) still say an operator-registered identity provider admits under `invite_only`, without the `allowJit` condition.
  - `packages/spec/**` is outside the dev's file surface ("stop and tell the seat"), so the dev could not edit it. The dev did not raise it either.
  - The seat decides: widen the surface for a docblock-only edit in this PR, or file a follow-up. The seat or the maintainer also decides whether a semantic migration entry is owed, following the `18.audience-posture-default-invite-only` precedent.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-xykd7v`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5p3T5YWhLjurajudnQ`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `657009a2fd032beba672fe74b12043b0b180bd29`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-membership-admission.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-sign-in-options.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/objectql-adapter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-schema-config.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts, content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx

Delta round over the FAIL record 6719336371 (head `9c8e1977`). Inputs, and only these: card #30967 with every comment (triage 6687843375, serial wait 6702286087, options 6710967585, ruling record 6718355623, claim 6718397620, dev report 6719252885, claim amendment 6719345374); PR #31448's body, its 26-file list, its comments and the net diff `origin/main...657009a2`; the 65 check-runs on this head. The vendor was read in the published `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 tarball (the version `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json` pins), read only, nothing run. The PR's own commits since the FAILed head are `53145b30` (changeset to patch + none), `40589c88` (changeset to minor + semantic, the two spec docblocks, the pre-fill pin), `8fd814df` (merge of `origin/main`) and `657009a2` (pt-BR strings).

**Gates on this head, as read:** 65 check-runs, 57 success, 8 skipped (opt-in and schedule-only jobs), 0 failure, 0 in progress. Every required context is success: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core (and all 8 shards), Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check UI, Test UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate; Lint UI is skipped by its paths filter. Check Changeset is success. The earlier record's "no test, type-check, lint or build family has answered" is no longer true: all of them have, green.

**The earlier record's findings, one by one:**

- must-fix, changeset level and kind (.changeset/30967-sso-sign-in-options.md): **resolved** by `40589c88`. The committed changeset grades `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` `minor` and declares `Clause-②: yes (widening)` plus `Metadata-protocol: semantic`; the PR body carries the same two lines. The intermediate `53145b30` (patch + none) is superseded in the tree. Check Changeset is success on this head.
- should-fix, sys-sso-provider.object.ts:281-283 Setup pre-fill: **resolved** by the three-row pin added to sso-register-platform-admin-gate.test.ts in `40589c88`. It writes `1`, `0` and `NULL` into both columns below better-auth, asserts the engine read the data API serves presents `true`, `false` and `null`, builds the body as the Console seeds a field-backed param (`rowDefault ?? param.defaultValue ?? field.defaultValue`, which is the live rule at ui/packages/fields/src/resolveActionParams.ts:890), posts it through the real `/sso/update-provider`, and reads the stored value back. The residual is that the pin models the Console's seeding rule rather than driving the Console; the rule it models is the one in the tree, so the finding is closed.
- should-fix, ADR-0011 stale sentence: **disposed by a carrier**. The claim amendment 6719345374 carries it as a separate card, and card #31452 (opened 2026-11-08T08:37Z, "ADR-0011's identity-action census says one identity action is unassessed; sys_sso_provider.edit_sso_sign_in_options makes it two") exists and is open. Not owed in this PR; ADR-0011 is a governed surface.
- should-fix, the published spec misstating `invite_only`: **resolved** by `40589c88`. Both docblocks in auth-config.zod.ts (`audiencePermitsSelfRegistration`, and the `posture` member of `AudienceConfigSchema`) now state the `allowJit` condition, off by default, with `oidcProviders` entries unchanged. Docblock text only, no schema, type, default or export moved, under the surface the claim amendment widened. The `.describe()` string on `posture` ("invite_only (default — operator acts only)") is unchanged and still true: turning `allowJit` on is an operator act.
- nit, oidcConfig fingerprint: **carried**, still a nit (below).
- nit, org-admin writers on Setup-registered providers: **carried**, still a nit (below).

### ① Derived judgments

(a) **Accept set widened on two REST bodies, non-protocol: right.** `POST /api/v1/auth/sso/register` and `POST /api/v1/auth/sso/update-provider` now accept `allowIdpInitiated` and `allowJit` as `@better-auth/sso` provider `additionalFields` (sso-sign-in-options.ts `SSO_PROVIDER_SIGN_IN_FIELDS`, handed over at auth-manager-plugin-list.ts `schema.ssoProvider.additionalFields`). In the vendor, `parseSSOProviderAdditionalFields` (index.mjs:1847) is the one door, typed `boolean`, so a non-boolean is 400. This is the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` the PR declares. No new writer population: register stays behind plugin-auth's platform-admin gate, update-provider behind `sessionMiddleware` + `checkProviderAccess` (index.mjs:2270: the provider's `userId`, or an org owner or admin when the row carries `organizationId`) plus plugin-auth's held-caller refusal.

(b) **The meaning of an authorable key moved: right, and declared.** `auth.audience.posture: 'invite_only'` (`system.AuthConfig.audience`) now admits an uninvited `@better-auth/sso` sign-in only when that provider's `allowJit` is on. The spec docblocks say so; `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is the gate's own name for it; the changeset states the behaviour change and the escape hatch, which is what the ruling required. The spec's schema, default (`invite_only`), accept set and exports are unchanged, so `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface` and `check:docs` have nothing to project (no `.describe()` moved), and all are green.

(c) **Default off, refused when off, per provider: right.** `allow_idp_initiated` and `allow_jit` are `Field.boolean({ defaultValue: false, trackHistory: true })`, and the vendor declaration has `defaultValue: false`. SAML: the vendor reads `options?.saml?.allowIdpInitiated` inside the ACS handler body (index.mjs:2939) and judges it in `validateInResponseTo` (index.mjs:1506-1545), so the getter in `ssoSamlOptions()` is read per request; it answers the `AsyncLocalStorage` scope `runSsoCallback` opens for `POST /sso/saml2/sp/acs/:providerId` only (`ssoCallbackOf`, sso-oidc-refusal-cause.ts:358-362), and `false` with no scope. OIDC: `bounceIfIdpInitiated` reads `provider.oidcConfig.allowIdpInitiated` off the row (index.mjs:4134), which the adapter's read half sets from that row's own column on `findOne` and `findMany`. Off answers as today: SAML `unsolicited_response`, OIDC `state_not_found`.

(d) **A stored blob member cannot override the column: right.** `applyIdpInitiatedToOidcConfigOnRead` overwrites the member unconditionally; `stripIdpInitiatedFromOidcConfigOnWrite` runs on `create`, `update` and `updateMany`, after `remapKeys(camelToSnake)`, so the rows are in snake_case where both halves read `oidc_config` and `allow_idp_initiated`. The strip takes nothing an author could write away: the vendor's own register and update schemas already strip that member from a body.

(e) **`invite_only` refusal before any row is written: right.** The gate runs in better-auth's `validateUserInfo` path, before the user insert; a refusal writes no user, account or session, and the vendor rethrows `SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED` to the redirect's `error=`.

(f) **Every change audited: right.** Both fields are `trackHistory`; adapter writes go through `withSystemContext`, whose write context is `authSystemWriteContext()`, so the ledger row names the human who called update-provider.

(g) **New platform-object action and list columns: right.** `edit_sso_sign_in_options` (POST, `target: '/api/v1/auth/sso/update-provider'`, three `defaultFromRow` params, no `ai` block) and the two new `all` list-view columns. Human-only under ADR-0011 bucket H's own test; the census sentence is #31452's.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` `minor`, `@objectstack/platform-objects` `minor`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. PR body: the same two lines. Both match what the diff publishes: items 1 and 2 are new toggles that widen who can sign in (widening, default off); item 4 moves the meaning of `invite_only` for every deployment with an `@better-auth/sso` provider (semantic, which takes at least `minor` on a moved package, and both moved packages are `minor`). Check Changeset is success. The earlier must-fix is closed.
- **Behaviour-change statement:** the ruling's requirement is met. The changeset's first body paragraph says plainly that uninvited SSO sign-ins under `invite_only` (the default) are now refused with `SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED`, that no user is created, that the account used to be created, and it names the per-provider `allowJit` escape hatch with both the Setup path and the REST call, and the unchanged cases.
- **should-fix — `@objectstack/spec` has no changeset entry.** The diff moves `packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts` (docblock text only). The TSDoc on `audiencePermitsSelfRegistration` and on the `posture` member ships in the package's `dist/*.d.ts`, so the released package changes, and Post-Task Checklist step 3 asks for a changeset for anything that publishes; the precedent the level gate's own docblock records (#16347) graded `@objectstack/spec` `patch` for one re-worded TSDoc.
